findings.text: A schedulable unit carries an atomic word encoding state plus location, a doubly linked queue node, and a callback pointer invoked by a worker; when lock validation is enabled an additional dependency map is present for ordering checks.
A timer deferred unit embeds a base work item, a timer object, a destination queue pointer selected at expiry, and an integer CPU hint indicating where the timer should place the work.
An RCU deferred unit embeds a base work item, an RCU grace period head, and a destination queue pointer used once the grace period elapses.

Queue attributes combine a scheduler niceness, an allowed CPU set that pools must match, an internal per pod subset used for locality, a strict flag controlling whether workers may migrate outside the pod set, an affinity scope selector, and an ordering flag requiring serial in order execution.

Signal file descriptor payload is a fixed width record describing signal number, error, code, sender process and thread identity, user identity, file descriptor, band, overrun, trap number, status, integer and pointer values, user and system times, fault address with address precision, system call number with call address and architecture, padded to 128 bytes to keep read size stable across versions.
A synchronous execution wrapper contains only an embedded base work item used to run a function on a chosen CPU.

The atomic state word uses low bits for pending, inactive, pool queue pointer present, and linked successor indications, plus an optional static initialization marker under object debugging; above them sit 4 flush color bits, and when the pointer present bit is set the remaining high bits hold a pool queue address requiring coarse alignment to preserve color and flag space.

When the pointer present indication is clear the high portion of the state word instead encodes bottom half execution request, a 16 bit disable nesting depth, and a capped pool identifier with the all ones value meaning no previous pool, leaving the low flag bits unchanged.

Fresh initialization stores a state meaning no pool, clears queue linkage to an empty list, records the supplied callback, and optionally establishes a lock dependency map which is omitted when validation is off; static declaration additionally marks the object as statically allocated while stack variants record on stack origin, keyed stack init accepts a caller supplied lock class, and stack destroy helpers are no operation in this configuration.

Delayed initialization first prepares the embedded base item then arms timer state as interrupt safe, with deferrable variants requesting timer deferral during idle; on stack forms use stack aware timer setup; RCU initialization only prepares the embedded base item leaving grace period handling to the queuer.

Ordered allocation requests an unbound queue with internal ordered marking and concurrency of 1; legacy creation helpers map to unbound or per CPU selections with memory reclaim and optional freezable behavior while preserving legacy markings.

Untargeted queue and modify operations default to an unbound CPU selector; scheduling helpers direct work to the default per CPU system queue, with CPU specific forms honoring the caller supplied processor and delayed forms forwarding an expiration interval.
Conditional reactivation only enqueues when enabling succeeds and reports success accordingly, otherwise leaving the item disabled and reporting failure without queuing.

Pending status is determined by inspecting the pending bit inside the atomic state word, with delayed status delegating to the embedded base item and static status reflecting the static marker where object debugging exists else always false.

Compatibility fetch from user space copies only owner, group and mode into kernel permission state and signals a fault error if user access fails; conversion back to user layouts publishes key, owner, group, creator identities, mode and sequence, with legacy layout applying identifier translation helpers.

The IPC orphan control delegates integer vector handling to the generic minimum maximum handler then, on successful writes that leave forced removal enabled, triggers destruction of orphaned shared memory segments in the enclosing namespace.

Orphan destruction serializes against identifier table changes with a write semaphore on the shared memory identifier set and, only when entries remain in use, holds RCU read protection while iterating the identifier radix structure.

Work state is conveyed through an atomic long accessed via bit test operations, allowing pending and static queries and flag manipulation without holding a sleepable lock; queue linkage itself is managed by queuing paths outside these fragments.

An item starts idle with no pool, becomes pending when queued with either a pool queue pointer plus flush color or off queue disable and pool history, may chain a linked successor, and returns to idle after execution with inactivity marking preventing requeue while disabled.

Flush generations cycle through 16 color values stored in the state word, letting a flush operation advance the active color and wait until items carrying prior colors drain while newly queued items adopt the new color.

Allocation helpers create normal, device managed, ordered, attribute based, and legacy queues with format names, flag sets, concurrency limits and lock maps, funneling through profiling hook wrappers.

Queuing services expose immediate, delayed and modify delayed submission, per CPU and system default scheduling, conditional enable plus queue, and queue flushing with system wide warnings; CPU execution helpers either invoke directly when workqueues are unavailable or dispatch through a keyed helper.

Compatibility and IPC services expose user to kernel permission fetch, kernel to user permission publish in two layouts, orphan aware sysctl integer handling with forced removal, orphan destruction across a namespace, and generic bounded integer vector sysctl handling.

Utility helpers expose container conversions between base work and delayed, RCU and caller structures, sysfs registration returning success in this configuration, and a no operation watchdog touch for a given CPU.
Worker threads transfer control to the callback stored in each item, receiving the work item pointer so the handler can recover its enclosing structure and perform the deferred action.

Timer expiry for delayed items and RCU grace completion for RCU items act as asynchronous entry points that route the embedded work to its recorded queue and CPU; sysctl writes to the orphan control act as an administrative entry that may trigger reclamation.

Flushing globally shared system queues risks stalling unrelated subsystems and deadlock when called from within work context, so the flushing wrappers emit a warning whenever a compile time recognizable system queue is targeted.

Misaligned pool queue allocation would corrupt color and flag bits, pool identifiers beyond the capped width collapse to the no pool sentinel losing history, and unbounded disable nesting can overflow the 16 bit depth field.

Compatibility fetch trusts user pointers and must validate access to avoid faulting on bad addresses, while bottom half queues accept only a narrow flag subset so requesting blocking features like freezable or reclaim would violate execution context constraints.

Pending occupies position 0, inactive 1, pool pointer present 2, linked 3, with an optional static bit under debugging; 4 color bits follow the flag field, off queue flags occupy 1 bit, disable depth 16 bits, and pool identity uses remaining bits capped at 31.

Color count is 16, unbound CPU selector equals the configured CPU count, busy query uses bit 0 for pending and bit 1 for running, worker description is limited to 32 characters, queue behavior flags span bits 0 through 8 plus internal bits 15 through 19 with bottom half queues restricted to bottom half high priority and per CPU, and concurrency defaults are 2048 maximum with half as default and 8 as minimum.

Stack state uses 1 for on stack and 2 for disabled with the top bit of an unsigned 32 bit word requesting automatic disarm during handling and serving as the sole valid flag bit; signal file descriptor close on exec and nonblock values alias the standard open flags and the info record is fixed at 128 bytes.

Affinity scope enumerates default, per CPU, per SMT thread, per last level cache, per cache shard, per NUMA node, per system, then a count sentinel; workqueue type and user signal headers carry conventional include guards.
